rationale: All five prior blocking findings (CR-001..CR-005) are resolved against current source: ordering helpers moved to index_group_ordering.py with annotations and tests, Optional replaced by X | None, and the archive, reactivation and re-select statements now have compiled-SQL assertions. Deferred DF-001 and DF-002 were not re-checked; no new findings are discovered on this round.

findings.title: Group-ordering helpers appended to oversized module
findings.problem: code-quality.md Module Cohesion says not to append a new concern to a module of about 500 lines or more. The file was 513 lines and is now 603. _naive_utc, _none_first, _row_order_key and _order_index_groups are standalone pure functions added at module level.
findings.impact: Documented standard is broken by newly written code and further inflates a module the guide wants split.
findings.recommendation: Move the group-ordering helpers into their own module next to the service, import them from stale_datasource_service.py, and move their tests with them.
findings.check_notes: Helpers moved to index_group_ordering.py (order_index_groups); service module now 578 lines; tests moved to test_index_group_ordering.py

fix.change: Moved group-ordering helpers into new index_group_ordering.py (public order_index_groups); service imports it

findings.title: _none_first lacks type annotations
findings.problem: code-quality.md requires explicit parameter and return types in new code. _none_first(value) has neither.
findings.impact: Documented standard is broken by newly written code.
findings.recommendation: Annotate it, e.g. def _none_first(value: datetime | None) -> tuple[int, datetime | None], matching its actual return.
findings.check_notes: _none_first annotated (date | None) -> tuple[int, date | None]; _row_order_key also annotated

fix.change: Annotated _none_first as (date | None) -> tuple[int, date | None], and _row_order_key return type

findings.title: New signatures use Optional instead of X | None
findings.problem: code-quality.md prefers X | None over typing.Optional[X]. The signatures this change added or rewrote (_fetch_activity_signals, _evaluate_staleness, _idle_stale_stmt, _recheck_rows, _process_stale_group) use Optional[datetime] and Optional[list[str]]. The module already has from __future__ import annotations.
findings.impact: Documented standard is broken by newly written code.
findings.recommendation: Replace Optional[X] with X | None in the signatures this change added or rewrote.
findings.check_notes: typing.Optional import removed; no Optional remains in the service module; signatures use X | None

fix.change: Replaced Optional[X] with X | None across the service module and dropped the typing import

findings.title: Archive and reactivation UPDATE targets untested
findings.problem: The reactivation and archive UPDATEs run against a mocked session.execute. The reactivation test only checks that the substrings 'marked_stale_at' and 'lifecycle_state' appear in str(statement), and lifecycle_state is also in the WHERE clause. The archive UPDATE is never compiled. No test in tests/codemie/service/stale_datasource asserts the ACTIVE or ARCHIVED value or the lifecycle_state == STALE guard.
findings.impact: A regression that reactivates rows into the wrong state, archives rows as the wrong state, or drops the STALE guard protecting rows moved to ACTIVE by complete_progress() would pass the suite.
findings.recommendation: In the reactivation test, compile the UPDATE and assert it sets lifecycle_state=ACTIVE and marked_stale_at=None with the STALE guard and the group's ids. In the happy-path test, compile the last execute call and assert lifecycle_state=ARCHIVED, the group's ids and the STALE guard.
findings.check_notes: Archive and reactivation tests compile the UPDATE and assert ARCHIVED/ACTIVE values, marked_stale_at None, ids and STALE guard; match source sa_update calls

fix.change: Reactivation and archive tests now compile the UPDATE and assert target state, ids and STALE guard

findings.title: Per-group re-select statement untested
findings.problem: _idle_stale_stmt(ids) is the per-group re-select behind the len(rows) < len(row_ids) guard. It is only exercised through a mocked session.execute that returns hand-picked rows, so the id IN filter and the completed, is_fetching, is_queued and error predicates are never observed. Nothing in the tests references _idle_stale_stmt.
findings.impact: If the ids filter or an idle predicate were dropped, the re-select could return rows mid-reindex or in error state, or the whole STALE table, and the walk would delete indexes the old query excluded, with every test still green.
findings.recommendation: Compile StaleDatasourceService._idle_stale_stmt(['a','b']) and assert the id IN param plus the STALE, completed, is_fetching, is_queued and error predicates. Assert that _idle_stale_stmt() without ids has no id filter.
findings.check_notes: TestIdleStaleStmt compiles _idle_stale_stmt and asserts STALE, completed, is_fetching, is_queued, error predicates and id IN filter, plus no-ids case

fix.change: Added TestIdleStaleStmt compiling _idle_stale_stmt with and without ids

deferred.title: Shared-index guard snapshot is never refreshed
deferred.problem: active_index_names is computed once, so an ACTIVE datasource that adopts a candidate index mid-walk is not noticed and the index is deleted. The longer walk with per-group commits widens the window.
deferred.preexisting: The one-time ACTIVE snapshot guard predates this change and was left unchanged.

deferred.title: Archive counts and metrics ignore UPDATE rowcount
deferred.problem: indexes_deleted, datasources_archived and the metrics use len(archive_ids), not the STALE-guarded UPDATE's rowcount, so a row flipped to ACTIVE by complete_progress() is still counted after the ES delete.
deferred.preexisting: The old sweep also counted from row lists after the ES delete and did not read the UPDATE rowcount.

standards_review.notes: 5 commit subjects in the review range all match the documented EPMCDME-####: Description format
New code uses Optional[...] instead of X | None, _none_first has no annotations, and ~90 lines of ordering helpers were appended to a module that grew from 513 to 603 lines.
No auth, secret, untrusted-input or logging-of-sensitive-value issues found in the changed source; logs carry index names and datasource ids only

final_round.rationale: Source behaves as specced and all 14 criteria pass, but two documented code-quality standards are broken (annotations, module cohesion) and the new UPDATE and re-select statements have no asserting tests. 2 deferred (stale shared-index snapshot, archive counts from ids not rowcount; see code-review-deferred.local.md); about 9 lens claims filtered as noise or by-design (single up-front signal fetch per AC3, tz handling kept from detection, test brittleness).
